clue.text: Neighbour appears in the garden

definitions.note: a phrase placing the thing rather than naming it, fair because the garden feature is found nowhere else

blocks.note: first meaning: to lie alongside, as one country does another
second meaning: a long flower bed running along the edge of a lawn

explanation.surface: The person from next door turns up in your garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' reads as a noun, a person, but it is the verb meaning to adjoin.
explanation.definitionFit: Countries that adjoin each other share a frontier, and gardeners call the planted strip edging a lawn the same word.

clue.text: Shot by university player was highly rated

blocks.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge
a chip is a short lofted shot in golf or football

explanation.surface: A stroke played by a varsity sportsman earns high praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue comes first and the shot follows it: 'by' means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are those of the most reliable, prestigious companies, so anything so described is held in top regard.

clue.text: Comes back in tears about ... about missing both start and finish

indicators.note: dropping the first and last letters leaves only the inner part of the word before it
something placed about another surrounds it, so one set of letters wraps the other

blocks.note: to rend is to tear apart
the word about, shorn of its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone returns weeping about some unnamed matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis hides that the first 'about' is the wrapping signal and the second is raw material to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that rebounds springs back after striking something, so it returns to where it started.

clue.text: Bird found in, for example, central Crete

indicators.note: the central part of a word is what remains between its first and last letters

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation, from Latin exempli gratia
the inner three letters of the island's name

explanation.surface: A kind of bird is to be seen in the middle of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: This white wading heron is a common sight around Mediterranean marshes and coasts.

clue.text: Does it in different publications

indicators.note: made different, the letters are set in another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone produces various printed works.
explanation.definitionFit: Each separately printed issue or version of a book or newspaper is a distinct release from the press.

clue.text: Impartial insider tested new arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement puts the same letters in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A neutral company insider has trialled a fresh layout.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no personal stake in the outcome can judge fairly, taking neither side.

clue.text: A striking performer?

blocks.note: surface reading: an eye-catching, impressive entertainer
setter's reading: one who strikes the floor with metal-tipped shoes while dancing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests looking remarkable; here it is literal hitting, of the stage with the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: This stage artist beats out rhythms by hitting the boards with metal plates fixed to the shoes.

clue.text: Sole means to get this type of ticket

blocks.note: sole means only, single
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: The only method of obtaining a particular kind of ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole means' reads naturally as a single phrase, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A single ticket, valid for the outward journey only, is described as such, as opposed to a return.

clue.text: Rest's disturbed by start of severe anxiety

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone
disturbed things are thrown out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word taken as written, without its apostrophe
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A person's sleep is broken by the first stirrings of serious worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental strain and tension from pressure are close synonyms of worry and nervousness.

clue.text: Colour of wood when left out

indicators.note: a letter that is out is no longer in the word

blocks.note: lumber is timber, sawn wood
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Asking what shade timber turns when it is abandoned outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown earth pigment gives its name to a dark reddish or yellowish-brown shade used by painters.

clue.text: "Go away", said rudely and very quietly to listener

blocks.note: dis is slang for insulting someone
pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music; with the a needed before it
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off, delivered rudely and in a whisper to whoever is listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in front of PP has no clue word of its own; it rides with 'very quietly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish or go out of sight is to leave a scene, as a quoted command might demand.

clue.text: Measures used, if anxious over return of spy

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece placed over comes first, on top
a return goes back the way it came, so each word is read from the end

blocks.note: stressed means anxious
to snoop is to spy

explanation.surface: Steps taken in case someone nervous about a returning agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' applies to both words, each turned round where it stands, rather than to the pair as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes use these as units of volume, each spoon holding about ten millilitres of a liquid or powder.

clue.text: Doing business with her should be a pleasure

definitions.text: Doing business with her should be a pleasure

blocks.clueFragment: Doing business with her should be a pleasure
blocks.note: surface reading: the polite phrase about a dealer who is good to deal with
setter's reading: the pleasure is the very thing she sells

explanation.walkthrough: The stock business phrase 'a pleasure doing business with you' turns literal: her trade is pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress kept by wealthy or aristocratic clients, she earned her living by offering company and sex.

clue.text: Collect a large quantity

blocks.note: first meaning: to gather together, accumulate
second meaning, read as two words: a, and mass for a great amount

explanation.surface: Gather up lots of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into two words, A MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or hoard is to gather; and a mass is a large body or heap, here preceded by the article.

clue.text: Coolness towards fashionable mark of distinction

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
a difference is what distinguishes one thing from another

explanation.surface: Someone's frosty attitude to a trendy badge of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark of distinction' sounds like an honour; read flatly, a distinction is just a difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool attitude shows lack of interest or concern, the same emotional detachment as apathy.

clue.text: Grace and Fran produced a bouquet

indicators.note: the names are worked up into something new, their letters remade

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women made up a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' means a bunch of flowers in the surface, but here it is the scent, as of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic aroma, a pleasant smell or perfume.

clue.text: Offended by misrepresentation of Tudor Age

indicators.note: a misrepresentation shows things wrongly, so the letters are set out wrongly too

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A historian upset by a distorted portrayal of Henry VIII's era.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor Age is the period of English history under the Tudor monarchs, 1485 to 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scandalised or indignant is a stronger form of being insulted or hurt by something.

clue.text: Put two and two together and it gets round about journalist being on drugs

indicators.note: something that gets round another encircles it

blocks.note: putting numbers together is adding them
taken as written
c for circa, about
ed, short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone works out the truth: a reporter has a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put two and two together' means deduce, but here it is plain arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked or dependent on a substance needs it habitually, so is under its control.

clue.text: Scene of conflict as Sussex town is reduced to dust

blocks.note: Battle is the East Sussex town by the site of the 1066 Battle of Hastings
what is ground has been crushed fine

explanation.surface: A war zone where a Sussex town has been flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: The town named after the Battle of Hastings fits the warlike surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where armies meet, or any arena of dispute, is where the fighting takes place.

clue.text: Watch the German return and get cross

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the German article is read backwards

blocks.note: to watch is to see
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Seeing a German come back makes someone angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes losing one's temper suddenly, as a bull is supposed to at a red cape.

clue.text: Examines ropes twisted around bed head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
a twisted thing is bent out of shape, so the letters lose their order
the rearranged letters go around the single letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone checks tangled cords looped around the top of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate thoroughly, poking into a matter as a surgeon's instrument does.

clue.text: It's a mistake to express hesitation or turn and run

indicators.note: to turn the word or is to swing it round to face backwards

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitating
taken as written
r is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A warning that dithering, or turning tail, would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like the joining word between two choices, but it is a piece itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip, blunder or wrong action is exactly what is meant by a mistake.

clue.text: Blend of port I pour drunkenly

indicators.note: a drunk pours unsteadily, so the letters spill out in a muddle

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mix of fortified wine sloshed out by a tipsy pourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a mix of dried petals, it also means any medley or miscellany of assorted things.

clue.text: Proposal of judge overturned

indicators.note: in a down entry, overturning a word turns it upside down, reading it from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
a ref, or referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A judge's suggestion has been reversed on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a mere link word, but it supplies the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is something put forward for acceptance, such as a bid or suggestion.

clue.text: Forest-dweller makes bird take cover

blocks.note: a small red-breasted songbird
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A woodland creature causes a bird to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw lived with his band of merry men in Sherwood, so he dwelt in a forest.

clue.text: Oppose steps to get rid of student

indicators.note: getting rid of something means it is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a flight is a set of stairs
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone resisting the moves taken to expel a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like measures or actions, but it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight a proposal is to resist and contest it, struggling against it.

clue.text: Scatter after girl's mad spree

indicators.note: something mad is wild and disordered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name, with its possessive s
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: People run off in all directions after a woman's crazy shopping binge.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to spread out and go off in different directions, as a crowd does.

clue.text: Sick deer do get destroyed

indicators.note: something sick is in a poor state, here letters out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Ill deer are bound to perish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn away gradually by wind or water has been ruined bit by bit.
